d.t: Simplified representation; reduction to a pattern or conventional form; abstraction; decorative generalization.
To represent (someone or something) in a particular style.

To represent (someone or something) abstractly in a conventional manner, commonly fancifully symbolic, to identify a particular item, by omitting most of the detail that is not unique to the item in question.
Made to conform to some style.
Represented according to some convention, omitting dispensable detail, rather than in a realistic or literal manner.
d.e: The symbol for the planet Mars is a stylized representation of the shield and spear of the god Mars.

d.t: A stylographic pen.
d.e: Malone put his stylo in his pocket. There was no use reporting a lunatic.

d.t: Any of the genus Stylosanthes of flowering plants.
Stylish; fashionable.
d.e: We so stylo, they just vile-o / We speak Singlish, awmost English-lah

d.t: The top step of the crepidoma, i.e. the platform upon which the superstructure of the building is erected.
d.e: The bases of the columns and the plinths below them appear to be standing on pedestals, but this is only an illusion, for the stylobate [translating Sockel] has been cut through in five places, and through each gap five steps lead up between the columns.

d.t: Resembling a stylus or pen.
Of or pertaining to the styloid process.
d.e: But is the human hyoid nevertheless absolutely deprived of the lateral parts of the skull? That is not the case. A ligament coming from each small callosity or from the apohyal is prolonged laterally and reaches the extremity of the styloid apophysis.

d.t: A statistical method of analyzing a text to determine its author.
d.e: Stylometry is a tool to be used when external evidence is lacking and the solution to the problem must come from the study of the texts which present the problem. Stylometry is therefore particularly useful in classical studies, especially for Greek texts which were written and…

d.t: A small synthesizer operated using a stylus.
An ancient writing implement consisting of a small rod with a pointed end for scratching letters on clay, wax-covered tablets or other surfaces, and a blunt end for obliterating them.
d.e: [T]he pleasure of writing on wax with a stylus is exemplified by the fine, flowing hand of a Roman scribe who made out the birth certificate of Herennia Gemella, born March 128 AD.

d.t: A hard-pointed pen-shaped instrument for marking on stencils used in a mimeograph machine.
A hard point, typically of diamond or sapphire, following a groove in a phonograph and transmitting the recorded sound for reproduction.
A tool for making small dots on a piece of heavy paper, used to produce Braille writing for the blind by hand.
Synonym of style.
A situation where an opponent's ball is directly in the way of one's own ball and the hole, on the putting green (abolished 1952).
An obstacle or obstruction.
d.e: Mary, will you be mine? Shall we go round together? Will you fix up a match with me on the links of life which shall end only when the Grim Reaper lays us both a stymie?

d.t: To thwart or stump; to cause to fail or to leave hopelessly puzzled, confused, or stuck.
d.e: They had lost the key, and the lock stymied the first three locksmiths they called.

d.t: To bring into the position of, or impede by, a stymie.
Bringing about contraction of tissues; harsh, raw, austere.
d.e: Boyles turns to look over his shoulder, squinting into the styptic sun, and then flags a hand over his head.

d.t: That stops bleeding; especially, in a minor way, topically.
d.e: The growth on top was a scrubby plant, unknown anywhere else on Malta, which was believed to have styptic qualities – it could staunch bleeding when packed on top of a wound […].

d.t: A substance used for styptic results.
d.e: The powdered gum with resin is used as a styptic; and the mucilage has been recommended as an application to burns.

d.t: An aromatic hydrocarbon; a colourless, oily liquid, used in the manufacture of polymers such as polystyrene.
d.e: He combined styrene with isobutylene, a volatile liquid, under pressure.

d.t: Of, from or relating to Styria.
A native or inhabitant of Styria.
Expanded polystyrene foam, such as is used in cups and packaging.
d.e: A while ago I read your column concerning the effects of hot tea on styrofoam cups.
